title: Universal and rigorous asymptotic convergence of standard macroscopic quantum electrodynamics to the modified Langevin noise formalism
abstract: The standard Langevin noise formalism (LNF) is a well-established approach for macroscopic quantum electrodynamics in unbounded lossy media, and accordingly, its application to finite objects requires endowing the surrounding vacuum with a fictitious absorption that is taken to asymptotically vanish. Existing justifications for such a singular limiting procedure have been mainly restricted to phenomena governed by vacuum fluctuations and medium-induced interactions (Casimir-Polder forces, thermal radiation, quantum emitter dynamics, etc.), thereby strictly excluding scenarios that involve the scattering of external quantum radiation. Conversely, the modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF) has recently been established as the complete canonical quantum theory for arbitrary macroscopic systems and electromagnetic processes, entirely bypassing the need for limiting procedures, treating incident quantum radiation fields as independent degrees of freedom, and exactly reducing to the LNF for unbounded media. In this work, we demonstrate that the LNF limiting procedure is universally valid by showing that it recovers any physical prediction of the MLNF across all regimes, including arbitrary quantum scattering processes. Specifically, we introduce a suitable mapping associating any MLNF state and observable with a corresponding entity within the LNF augmented by fictitious vacuum absorption. We then rigorously prove that, as the fictitious absorption tends to zero, every LNF matrix element constructed via this mapping exactly converges to its MLNF original, so that the limiting procedure establishes the asymptotic convergence of the LNF to the MLNF.
summary: This paper establishes the rigorous mathematical link between two formalisms for quantum electrodynamics: the standard Langevin noise formalism (LNF) and the more general modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF). By constructing a precise mapping and proving the convergence of matrix elements, the authors demonstrate that the LNF is asymptotically valid even for complex scenarios like external quantum scattering, resolving key theoretical limitations in the field.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously prove the universal asymptotic convergence of the standard Langevin noise formalism (LNF) to the more complete modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF) in macroscopic quantum electrodynamics.
main_result: It is rigorously shown that the LNF limiting procedure is universally valid because it recovers all physical predictions of the MLNF across all regimes, including complex quantum scattering processes.
method: The authors introduce a suitable mapping between MLNF states/observables and LNF entities augmented by fictitious vacuum absorption, and then prove convergence by showing that LNF matrix elements exactly approach the MLNF original as the fictitious absorption vanishes.
model_or_system: The system is macroscopic quantum electrodynamics in lossy media, modeled using both the standard LNF (requiring fictitious absorption for finite objects) and the MLNF (a canonical theory treating incident radiation as independent degrees of freedom).
key_observables: Matrix elements of quantum observables, field operators (scattering, electric, magnetic polaritons), and expectation values of quantum states.
important_parameters: The fictitious absorption parameter ($\eta$), the limit $\eta 	o 0^+$, and the nature of the quantum scattering processes.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the mapping between the two formalisms is well-defined and that the interchange of the limit $\eta 	o 0^+$ with summations is mathematically rigorous.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the MLNF and shows LNF is a limit for unbounded media, then introduces the LNF($\eta$) framework, formalizes the limiting procedure, maps the MLNF scattering sector into LNF($\eta$), and finally proves the universal asymptotic convergence via matrix element analysis.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial, rigorous mathematical foundation for applying standard quantum electrodynamics techniques (LNF) to complex, finite systems involving external quantum fields, resolving long-standing theoretical ambiguities.
